MAIN ANALYSIS DONE (associational throughout; unweighted sample statistics). Headline: the jailed/not shortfall is **large at every baseline asset level and roughly constant in proportional terms**; what grows with baseline is the **dollar** size of the gap, and that growth is what a constant proportional gap produces mechanically, so I am **not** claiming a steeper hit at any one income level. Two things you asked to be told loudly are at the bottom of this message.

**TABLE 1 — PRIMARY: 1996 wealth, jailed vs never-jailed, within 1985 asset stratum (black males; inference population)**

| Stratum | ver | n_j / n_n | med96 J / N | ABS gap (median) [95% CI] | mean J / N | ABS gap (mean) | REL ratio of means [95% CI] | log ratio | PS−0.5 [95% CI] | share>0 J/N |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| S1 | DEDUP | 40/305 | 0/5,150 | **−5,150** [−7,100,−3,900] | 11,622/45,219 | −33,597 | 0.257 [0.016,0.752] | −1.36 | +0.219 [0.134,0.295] | 35%/69% |
| S2 | DEDUP | 36/348 | 0/8,550 | **−8,550** [−12,000,−3,450] | 13,615/40,255 | −26,640 | 0.338 [0.159,0.602] | −1.08 | +0.139 [0.050,0.226] | 44%/72% |
| S3 | DEDUP | 37/440 | 6,500/28,905 | **−22,405** [−38,000,−12,000] | 17,338/103,511 | −86,174 | 0.167 [0.076,0.319] | −1.79 | +0.205 [0.134,0.272] | 59%/80% |

PS = P(never-jailed > jailed) − 0.5. Rank-gap p-values (AS-IS): S1 0.0002, S2 0.0016, S3 0.0006. Pooled stratified van Elteren: z = −6.13, p = 8.6e-10 (dedup z = −6.55, p = 6.0e-11). **Honest caveat:** the within-stratum dollar-median permutation p-values are *not* significant individually (S1 p=1.00, S2 p=0.10, S3 p=0.13) — medians are degenerate at $0 in the bottom two strata and n_jailed is 38–63. The robust evidence is the rank gap and the log-ratio, not the raw within-stratum dollar gaps.

**TABLE 5 — the interaction, formally (labels permuted WITHIN stratum)**
| Gap measure | as-is S1→S2→S3 | p_trend | p_het | dedup S1→S2→S3 | p_trend | p_het |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ABS diff of means ($) | −19,408/−26,921/−86,395 | 0.179 | 0.249 | −33,597/−26,640/−86,174 | 0.280 | 0.349 |
| ABS diff of medians ($) | 0/−7,200/−22,650 | 0.125 | 0.176 | −5,150/−8,550/−22,405 | 0.225 | 0.292 |
| REL log ratio of means | −1.29/−1.20/−1.81 | 0.458 | 0.571 | −1.36/−1.08/−1.79 | 0.518 | 0.523 |
| REL rank gap PS−0.5 | +0.134/+0.154/+0.208 | 0.217 | 0.447 | +0.219/+0.139/+0.205 | 0.841 | 0.474 |
| REL gap in share>0 | −0.199/−0.313/−0.224 | 0.797 | 0.471 | −0.342/−0.280/−0.210 | 0.223 | 0.472 |

**Nothing crosses p=0.05 for trend or heterogeneity.** The mechanism check matters: simulating a *constant* 0.3 proportional gap reproduces ratio ≈0.36 at both $27k and $103k scales while the dollar gap goes −$31k → −$118k. So "absolute gap widens, ratio shrinks" is largely mechanical, not two independent findings. A finer 5-bin cut (≤0, 1–2k, 2–6k, 6–15k, >15k) gives non-monotone ratios (0.28/0.19/0.36/0.12/0.23) with n_jailed 16–28 per bin — i.e. this file cannot resolve a gradient.

**TABLE 2 — baseline imbalance (your threat-to-validity point)**: unstratified black males start at d_asinh(1985) = −0.279 (p=0.07), median 800 vs 1,500. **Inside every stratum it collapses to |d_asinh| ≤ 0.14, all p ≥ 0.29** (S1 +0.03, S2 −0.11, S3 −0.14). Stratification does absorb the low start — it is not counted twice. Still confounded nonetheless: S3 spans $5k to $2.4M, and 1985 wealth may itself be pre-affected for men jailed in 1985.

**TABLE 3 — change-based / ratio-to-baseline (inflation handled)**: gap in median 1985→1996 change: S2 −6,880 [−9,525,−3,600], S3 −19,708 [−26,921,−9,400] (nominal $). Ratio-to-baseline (common inflation cancels in the contrast), S3: jailed median 96/85 = 0.139 vs never-jailed 1.640 → log ratio-of-ratios −2.47 [−3.74,−0.54], perm p = 0.0005. Direction is unambiguous: jailed medians are **flat or negative** in every stratum, never-jailed positive.

**Tertiary 1990** (descriptive only, inside the window): S3 jailed 13,650 → 3,350 → 6,250 vs never-jailed 14,000 → 16,400 → 28,900. Post-window change 1990→1996: jailed median 0 in all three strata — no recovery.

**Black females — descriptive only, excluded from inference (16 jailed as-is, 11 dedup; S2 n=2, S3 n=1)**: ALL-strata mean gap −39,607, ratio of means 0.081, PS 0.739, d_asinh −2.04 (p=0.001); direction same as males but no stratum is estimable.

**READ**: the shortfall tracks no particular income level — it is proportional and pervasive (~4–6× never-jailed/jailed mean wealth in every stratum; jailed wealth ranks lower 63–71% of the time). Baseline position buys no protection: even men with >$5k in 1985 who were jailed ended 1996 at a ratio of 0.16, the lowest in the table, though the trend tests cannot distinguish that from flat. The signature is **non-accumulation**, not depletion-then-recovery: jailed medians never rise across 1985→1990→1996 and stay at $0 in the lower strata.

**LOUD ITEM 1 — the S1 flip.** As-is, both S1 groups have median 1996 wealth = **$0**, so the bottom-stratum median gap is exactly **$0** (p=1.00) — readable as "no gap at the bottom." Dedup, never-jailed S1 median is **$5,150** and the gap is **−$5,150** (p=0.06). Cause: 1,703 of the 1,899 exact-duplicate rows are the single all-wealth-zero pattern, 196 never-jailed vs 23 jailed among black males, pinning the never-jailed median at zero. **The "no gap at the bottom" reading is an artifact of duplicated zero rows** — every other S1 measure (ratio 0.275, PS +0.134, share>0 −20pp) shows a bottom gap in both versions. The as-is version stays primary per your instruction; the deduped column sits beside it in Table 1.

**LOUD ITEM 2 — the relative-gap gradient is not stable.** The rank gap rises with baseline as-is (+0.134→+0.208) but is flat/reversed in dedup (+0.219→+0.205). Any "gradient" claim dies on that.

**DRAFT HYPOTHESIS (proxy baked in, no causal language)** — as written in `results_deliverable.md`: among black respondents, "income level" is **not measured** in this file (no income/earnings/wage/poverty/education/occupation/residence field) and is **proxied by pre-window asset position (composite_wealth_1985)**; on that basis black men with a jail spell recorded 1985–1994 hold roughly one-fifth the wealth of never-jailed black men by 1996 **at every level of baseline assets** (ratio of means 0.28/0.30/0.16 bottom→top; jailed wealth ranks lower 63–71% of the time), so the shortfall is nearly constant in proportional terms across the asset distribution rather than concentrated at one income level; its dollar size rises with baseline position (−$19k→−$27k→−$86k), which is what a constant proportional gap mechanically produces and which no trend test supports (p_trend ≥ 0.22); and it takes the form of **failure to accumulate** rather than visible depletion (jailed medians flat/negative in every stratum; S3 −$7,038 vs +$12,670, nominal; no recovery after the window). Unweighted, unadjusted association with a wealth proxy for income; selection into jail uncontrolled.

**LIMITATIONS**: no causal claim available or made; no survey weights, so unweighted sample statistics only; nominal dollars (only the 1985→1996 *change* levels are inflation-contaminated — the ratios cancel it); 1990 excluded from stratifier and covariate role; ever_jailed pools 1985–1994 with no timing/duration, and 1996 is ~2 years after window close; n_jailed 38–63 per stratum gives wide CIs (S1 and S2 ratio CIs include 0.02 and 0.14 respectively); black females not estimable by stratum; the residence-based incarceration proxy from study context is **inapplicable** — the file has no geography field (noted once per your instruction, not pursued).

payload.hypothesis: Among black respondents in this NLSY79 file, "income level" is not measured - the file contains no income, earnings, wage, poverty, education, occupation or residence field - so income level is proxied here by pre-window asset position (composite_wealth_1985), and on that basis: black men with a jail spell recorded between 1985 and 1994 hold roughly one-fifth the wealth of never-jailed black men by 1996 at every level of baseline assets (ratio of mean 1996 wealth 0.28, 0.30 and 0.16 across the bottom, middle and top 1985 asset strata; a jailed man's wealth ranks below a never-jailed man's 63-71% of the time), so the shortfall is nearly constant in proportional terms across the asset distribution rather than concentrated at one income level - with the shortfall's dollar size rising steeply with baseline position (-$19k to -$27k to -$86k), which is what a constant proportional gap mechanically produces rather than evidence of a steeper hit at the top, and which no formal trend test supports (p_trend >= 0.22) - and the shortfall takes the form of failure to accumulate rather than visible depletion, since jailed medians are flat or negative across 1985-1996 in every stratum (top stratum -$7,038 vs +$12,670, nominal dollars) and remain at or near zero after the jail window closes. This is an unweighted, unadjusted association of jail history with later wealth, stratified on a wealth proxy for income; selection into jail is not controlled, so it should not be read as an effect estimate.
payload.workflow: 1) Inspected the 6-column file (12,013 rows, 0 missing, no income/earnings/residence field) and confirmed 'income level' is unmeasured. 2) Restricted to race=='black'; inference population = black males (n=1465, 143 jailed); black females descriptive only (16 jailed). 3) Stratified on composite_wealth_1985 into <=0, 1-5000, >5000 (rank/tertile cut degenerate because 37.6% sit at exactly 0); 1990 wealth deliberately excluded from stratifier and covariate role as it lies inside the 1985-1994 jail window. 4) PRIMARY outcome = 1996 wealth level within stratum: medians, means, share with positive wealth, Hodges-Lehmann-free rank measure PS=P(never>jailed)-0.5, sign-preserving log (asinh(x/1000)) difference; 4,000-resample stratified bootstrap percentile CIs; two-sided permutation tests with each statistic centred on its own null (ratio null=1 i.e. tested on the log scale, PS null=0.5, differences null=0); Mann-Whitney and stratified van Elteren rank test; no OLS on raw skewed levels. 5) INTERACTION/TREND: per-stratum gaps in absolute (median, mean) and relative (log ratio of means, log ratio of p75, PS-0.5, gap in share>0) form; cross-stratum slope and heterogeneity tested by permuting jail labels WITHIN stratum (4,000 draws), plus a simulation showing dollar-gap widening is mechanical under a constant proportional gap. 6) SECONDARY: change 1985->1996 (nominal) and ratio-to-baseline so common inflation cancels in the contrast; TERTIARY: 1990 trajectory descriptive only. 7) BASELINE IMBALANCE: within-stratum 1985 jailed/not gaps with permutation tests. 8) SENSITIVITY: exact-duplicate removal reported side-by-side in every table, all-zero-cell removal, and a finer 5-bin stratification. Unweighted sample statistics throughout; associational language only.
